CIS1.name: Variable Name
CIS1.note: The variable name that replaces the CTDA's first argument. It trails a CTDA that uses a string parameter, and the CTDA's parameter 1 is then a very high value. [UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/CTDA Field. Seen in IDLE, PACK and CPTH.]

CIS2.name: Variable Name
CIS2.note: The variable name that replaces the CTDA's second argument. It trails a CTDA that uses a string parameter. [UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/CTDA Field. Seen in FACT, ENCH, SPEL, COBJ, QUST, IDLE, PACK, LSCR, PERK, SMBN, SMQN, SCEN and INFO.]

CTDA.name: Condition
CTDA.note: UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/CTDA Field. The condition reads as <Reference>.<Function>(<Param1>, <Param2>) <Operator> <Value>. [measured: every CTDA in Skyrim.esm is exactly 32 bytes, so Run On, Reference and the trailing index are all present — Fallout's CTDA has only the first two of the three, and its last two fields are optional.]

DESC.name: Description
DESC.note: UESP's lstring: an index into the game's string table, not a string of its own. The base's is Fallout's string. [measured: 4 bytes in every DESC field in Skyrim.esm]

DMDT.name: Destruction Stage Model Texture Hashes
DMDT.note: UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/ACTI. Skyrim's DMDT has a twelve-byte header — the version, the entry count and a flag — and then the texture entries, which is the same shape as its MODT. The base's is an array of Fallout texture hashes.

FULL.name: Full Name
FULL.note: UESP's lstring: an index into the game's string table, not a string of its own. The base's is Fallout's string. [measured: 4 bytes in every FULL field in Skyrim.esm]

MODT.name: Model Texture Hashes
MODT.note: The model's texture hashes. Skyrim's MODT comes in two forms. Most have a 12-byte header — a version of 2, the entry count and a zero — and then the entries; the rest have no header at all and the entries simply fill the field. Each entry is 12 bytes: a hash, the "dds" extension and a second hash. The first word says which form it is, so the header is read first and the rest follows the form it implies. [measured: 12,057 of Skyrim.esm's MODT fields have no header, and 8,538 have one; every field is a multiple of twelve, and the headered ones are twelve more than a multiple of twelve.]

struct.name: operator
struct.note: The upper 3 bits are the compare operator (0 = Equal to, 1 = Not equal to, 2 = Greater than, 3 = Greater than or equal to, 4 = Less than, 5 = Less than or equal to) and the lower 5 bits are flags: 0x01 = OR (otherwise conditions are ANDed together), 0x02 = Parameters (use aliases), 0x04 = Use global, 0x08 = Use Pack Data, 0x10 = Swap Subject and Target. The flags are mutually exclusive where noted: 0x02 and 0x08 both claim the parameters.

struct.name: unknown
struct.note: Unused data.

struct.name: comparison_value_raw
struct.note: The value the function result is compared against: a float, or a GLOB formid when the 0x04 Use global flag is set. Decoded here as a raw u32, the same as Fallout's.

struct.name: function
struct.note: The condition function's index. UESP's Skyrim function list gives the index as 'the index given on the above page, minus 4096'. Most Oblivion indices remain valid, and Skyrim adds hundreds more.

struct.name: padding
struct.note: Padding. The bytes are unused but may be non-zero.

struct.name: parameter1_raw
struct.note: The first parameter: a number, or a formid when the function takes one. Zero when the function needs no parameter. A string parameter is a CIS1 subrecord following the CTDA instead.

struct.name: parameter2_raw
struct.note: The second parameter, same shape as the first. A string parameter is a CIS2 subrecord following the CTDA instead.

struct.name: run_on
struct.note: How the condition applies: 0 = Subject, 1 = Target, 2 = Reference (see the reference field), 3 = Combat Target, 4 = Linked Reference, 5 = Quest Alias, 6 = Package Data, 7 = Event Data. Unlike Fallout's, this field is always present in Skyrim.

struct.name: reference_raw
struct.note: The function's reference — the formid the function is applied to, such as the target of an isDead check. Zero when no reference is needed. Always present in Skyrim.

struct.name: unknown2
struct.note: The index of the package data or quest alias to run on. -1 means 'none', and it is also used for other run-on types. This is Skyrim's extra trailing field: Fallout's CTDA is 20, 24 or 28 bytes, Skyrim's is always 32, the difference being this field plus Run On and Reference always being present. [measured: all 83,759 CTDA subrecords in Skyrim.esm are exactly 32 bytes]

struct.name: version
struct.note: Always 2 in the shipped data.

struct.name: count
struct.note: How many texture entries follow.

struct.name: extra_words
struct.note: How many four-byte words follow the texture entries.

struct.name: textures
struct.note: The destruction stage's textures.

struct.name: extra
struct.note: The words after the textures.

struct.name: textures
struct.note: The destruction stage's textures, with no header and no count.

struct.name: hash
struct.note: The texture's hash.

struct.name: extension
struct.note: The texture's file extension, which is "dds" in every shipped record.

struct.name: hash2
struct.note: A second hash.

struct.name: version
struct.note: Always 2 in the shipped data.

struct.note: How many texture entries follow.

struct.name: extra_words
struct.note: How many four-byte words follow the texture entries.

struct.name: textures
struct.note: The model's textures.

struct.name: extra
struct.note: The words after the textures. Their meaning is not documented.

struct.name: textures
struct.note: The model's textures, with no header and no count: the entries fill the field.

struct.name: hash
struct.note: The texture's hash.

struct.name: extension
struct.note: The texture's file extension, which is "dds" in all but a few hundred of the shipped entries.

struct.note: A second hash.

struct.note: The words after the textures. Their meaning is not documented.
